## Copied-feat integration review — completed; reference-code corrections required

**I found five concrete issues and prepared 11 exact before-and-after operations across four Python reference files.** The seven copied-feat contracts remain intact. No additional gameplay-rule change is required by these findings.

The proposed copies pass the existing helper assertions and the new adversarial tests. **Full cross-round Ready and the remaining world/runtime integrations are still unimplemented.**

Nothing was applied to the project, GitHub, index, registry or runtime flags. The supplied applied baseline remains **525 reviewed / 323 pending / 249 standalone / 173 interfaces**. The 39 previously accepted-but-unapplied spell identities remain separate from this code review.

:chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"}[Download the complete copied-feat review and correction archive](sandbox:/mnt/data/DD_Part5_Copied_Feat_Integration_Review_01.zip)

:chatgpt-content-reference{index="1"}[Read the complete source-linked review and individual case dispositions](sandbox:/mnt/data/DD_Part5_Copied_Feat_Integration_Review_01/REVIEW.md) · :chatgpt-content-reference{index="2"}[Read the Codex handoff](sandbox:/mnt/data/DD_Part5_Copied_Feat_Integration_Review_01/CODEX_HANDOFF.md) · :chatgpt-content-reference{index="3"}[Read the exact correction operations](sandbox:/mnt/data/DD_Part5_Copied_Feat_Integration_Review_01/CODE_OPERATIONS.json)

## 1. The five findings

| Finding | Reproduced original behavior | Proposed correction |
|---|---|---|
| **CFI-01 — Separate capture and class Reaction budgets** | Eldritch Echo capture spends the copy adapter’s Reaction, but the same Shaman still has `reactions = 1`, or the Mirrorsage still has `reaction = True`. | Bind capture to the **actual existing class Reaction account** and check current Reaction legality. Capture and class behavior now read and spend the same budget. |
| **CFI-02 — Reconstructing an adapter refreshes its cap** | A second adapter using the same owner, captures, RP, cadence, world and concentration ledger starts with an empty `release_rounds`, allowing another adapted copy in the same round. | Enforce one copy adapter per owner on the supplied canonical concentration ledger. Reuse its existing cap and receipts instead of constructing a fresh budget. |
| **CFI-03 — Stale native body/concentration state** | After commitment, an actual linked Shaman becoming unconscious still permits Mend to heal. A native concentration replacement can also leave the copy adapter granting Ward from an obsolete burden. | Check the current linked body at resolution. Reject unintegrated concentration drift **before payload, counter cleanup or clock mutation**, without overwriting the actual native source. |
| **CFI-04 — Step moves only one position representation** | A copied Step changes CopyWorld coordinates while the native Shaman remains at the old scalar position, so native aura checks can still grant eligibility from the old location. | Reject **this unsupported linked Shaman Step path before payment** until a canonical position adapter exists. Do not guess a mapping or silently leave the representations inconsistent. |
| **CFI-05 — Extra-turn identity can be reused as a regular start** | A completed extra-turn ID can be supplied as a new regular-start ID, advancing the ordinal and refreshing Reaction. | Reject IDs already recorded as extra turns, matching the existing protection in the opposite direction. |

These are reference-code enforcement and integration corrections, not new spells, class benefits or resource allowances. Their complete source references, affected functions, original behavior and boundaries are in `FINDINGS.json`.

### Reaction sharing: capture is not release

The correction makes **Eldritch Echo’s capture Reaction** use the actual Shaman/Mirrorsage account. It does not charge Mimicry a Reaction, create another Reaction or implement a Ready release.

Binding an already-spent account does not refill it. A genuinely supplied regular start refreshes the normal Reaction; an extra turn does not. The tests cover both directions: capture spending prevents a later use of that same Reaction, and an already-spent class Reaction prevents capture.

### Duplicate adapters: bounded protection, not persistence

The original adapted-Mend probe permits the RP sequence **44 → 42 → 40** through two adapters in the same numbered round. The second commitment should not acquire a fresh owner-wide allowance.

The proposed guard prevents that reconstruction **on the same actual canonical concentration ledger**. It does not solve save/load or protect against a caller manufacturing a different ledger and falsely calling it canonical. Durable owner identities and receipt restoration remain implementation requirements.

### Native state: no healing from an obsolete snapshot

In the original linked-body probe, the Shaman becomes unconscious after commitment, but the copy-world snapshot remains conscious. Mend then moves the recipient from **30 to 32 HP**.

The proposed resolver consults the linked body. A legally blocked result uses no payload RNG, performs no healing and refunds nothing. Components already performed at commitment are not demanded again.

For concentration divergence, the correction deliberately **rejects the unintegrated transition**. It does not pretend to understand, erase or recreate an unknown native concentration source. That transition still needs its actual adapter.

### Step: preserve the benefit while exposing the missing integration

The concrete fixture has the native Shaman at **0 feet** and its totem at **5 feet**. Copied Step moves the copy-world position to `[-15, 0, 0]`, but the original code leaves the native position at zero. The native aura query consequently still returns the totem as qualifying.

The proposed guard prevents that inconsistent result before consuming the Action, RP, permission or allowance.

**This is not a rule that Shaman cannot use Step.** The printed benefit remains. The missing work is an atomic position integration that updates the actual world state and its dependent queries.

The original `Shaman/step` history uses the separate, unlinked finite class-pool fixture. Its coordinate-only result remains valid within that narrower scope; it does not demonstrate the paid-totem Shaman position integration.

## 2. All seven profiles were assessed

| Profile | Disposition and retained boundary |
|---|---|
| **Strike** | Retain the native damage bound, actual caster attack and absence of additional critical copy dice. No original riders, external amplification or recursive-copy permission is added. |
| **Burst** | Retain the declared point, maximum three original recipients, one shared bounded damage pool and individual DEX outcomes. Later ineligibility does not authorize retargeting. |
| **Mend** | Retain actual eligible healing, willing living recipients, normal-HP/Critical caps and prohibitions. No revival, Wound cure, resource conversion or external healing-dice benefit is added. |
| **Ward** | Retain the actual single temporary-HP grant ledger, wasted rejected offers, concentration dependency and original deadline. Native concentration divergence now stops unsupported processing. |
| **Hindrance** | Retain WIS admission, Speed −10, no new Reactions, strongest-slow arbitration and the bounded future endpoint. No original hard-control rider or repeat save is copied. |
| **Boon** | Retain the implemented Shield-derived AC variant and strongest-family arbitration. The printed **next-attack and next-save variants remain required but unimplemented** source/consumption adapters. |
| **Step** | Retain the implemented Mist Step teleport component and its conditional coordinate checks. **Nonteleport movement remains an unimplemented printed variant**, and the true linked Shaman position path now fails closed. |

`PROFILE_DISPOSITIONS.json` includes every **complete profile**, the full common contract and source references.

The actual provider distinction remains important: a paid feat-only CHA credential permits **q0 only** and supplies no RP pool. It does not thereby qualify for all seven demonstrated native components. The delivered feat-only positive example is the rank-zero Strike route.

## 3. Shaman and Mirrorsage integrations: meaningful, but finite

**Shaman:** The supplied paid-totem test genuinely shares the Shaman’s RP, cadence and Action account. The feat copy receives no ordinary Shaman vent; a later qualifying ordinary Shaman spell can receive its own vent. A lasting copy displaces the actual totem burden at commitment, and countering afterward does not restore it.

The Bloodcaller restriction also remains correctly separated from an independently acquired CHA rank-zero feat route. The new corrections address the previously separate capture Reaction and the later body, concentration and position inconsistencies. They do not claim complete suppression, dispel, body-end or world synchronization.

**Mirrorsage:** The supplied tests genuinely use the shared `EchoLedger` allowance in both directions. A feat copy can prevent a later class-bound release, and a class summon/command/payment boundary can prevent the later feat copy. Repeated adapted copies use normal feat Refrain rather than the class’s first-release waiver; a countered commitment still spends the allowance.

Those cases retain their explicit prior-record premise. They do **not** execute complete class Mirrorbind/capture or the entire class Echo strain/payload procedure.

The release-only report’s earlier Shaman/Mirrorsage openings are therefore qualified by the later class package’s actual finite evidence. The historical reports remain unchanged; the current dispositions are recorded externally.

## 4. Every original history is preserved and dispositioned

The return contains individual dispositions for:

**19 release histories · 27 payload histories · 22 class histories · 7 Ready-lifecycle histories · 13 source acceptance examples**

All **68 complete ordinary histories** were independently replayed from the original source. Their full history and result objects match the archived reports—not merely their identifiers or counts.

`CASE_DISPOSITIONS.json` retains each complete original history, the complete baseline replay, the complete proposed replay and its individual assessment. No original history was rewritten.

The original cases remain coherent **at their disclosed inputs**. That does not establish that the original integrated code was correct in unsampled situations; the five findings demonstrate why those are different conclusions.

The seven Ready-lifecycle histories remain **already-paid-preparation-premise-only** evidence. Likewise, a processed `resolved: true` on a missed attack, prohibited heal or rejected buffer is not a claim that the requested hit, healing or grant succeeded.

## 5. Full cross-round Ready remains unimplemented

The existing proposed `COPY-READY-ALLOWANCE-01` wording is preserved exactly. This review does not reopen that choice or pretend it has been installed.

Its required behavior remains:

**Preparation** pays the actual casting transaction once and occupies the preparation round’s applicable allowances. **Same-round release** reuses that hold’s own tokens. **Later-round release** atomically checks and spends the later round’s feat allowance, an applicable **actually owned** Mirrorsage allowance and the real Reaction—without another RP, capture, component, strain, history or counter transaction.

The completed trigger precedes release. Targets and current geometry are selected at release under the fixed preparation choices. Original Ready and earlier capture deadlines remain binding. Invalid, declined or cap-blocked release cannot partially debit another ledger.

The supplied code does not implement that complete transaction:

- `CopyReleases.commit` and `ClassCopyCommit.commit` are direct-Action paths.
- `CopyPayloadReleases.declare` fixes direct-cast selection at declaration; `resolve` correctly prevents changing that paid direct selection.
- `CopyConcentration.committed(ready=True)` assumes prior payment, while `release_ready(actual_legal_release=True)` assumes the legality a complete implementation must actually establish.

**Setting that Boolean is not a Ready implementation.** The return’s `READY_GAP_MATRIX.json` identifies 12 missing integration areas and preserves the complete proposed rule beside them.

The copied-feat two-round allowance requirement must not be generalized to ordinary Ready or class Echo.

## 6. Exact proposed files

All files below are under `DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/tools/`.

| File | Original bytes | Proposed bytes | Operations |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `feat335_copy_capture.py` | 11,062 | 14,023 | 3 |
| `feat335_copy_release.py` | 13,155 | 13,697 | 2 |
| `feat335_copy_payloads.py` | 22,515 | 22,991 | 4 |
| `feat335_copy_class_release.py` | 9,978 | 12,386 | 2 |
| **Total** | | | **11** |

The archive supplies complete originals and proposed copies, full SHA256 bindings, exact replacement spans and full reverse reconstruction.

The prior **22-operation Control/Ready correction package is unchanged**. Its **13 feat-rule operations across four JSON files remain a separate proposed change set**. This return neither replaces that package nor applies those JSON operations.

## 7. Verification and retained holds

All three nested input archives match their supplied hashes and their actual bytes inside handoff03. Their **42/49/66 sources** produce **157 source-member records and 78 unique paths**. Every overlapping source is byte-identical.

The original helper suites reproduce **136, 115 and 205 assertions**. The class suite initially fails its hardcoded `C:/Github/DecenniumDescent` locator on this host; its successful replay used explicitly documented **in-memory path-only rebinding**, not rewritten source bytes.

The proposed copies pass all **456 existing helper assertions**, plus **47 new isolated tests with zero failures or errors**. The package also preserves full original/proposed before-and-after states for seven adversarial scenarios covering the five findings.

Separately, the read-only verifier passes **880 source, structural, complete-value and reference checks**, followed by **51 final return-member checks**. It verifies complete forward and reverse byte equality for all four corrected files.

**These are isolated reference-module executions, not a running game-engine validation.** No human gameplay or numerical-balance test was performed.

The existing whole positive-case holds remain **IN6-09-A, IN6-09-B, EN5-01-A, EN5-01-B and EN6-03-B**. No CR2 Undead, owner-level companion rating, donor CR inheritance or save-proficiency-to-Athletics conversion is invented. The separately completed Control15/Mental Prison semantic acceptance is not reopened.

Companion05 and Illusion13’s **16 accepted artifact files remain unchanged**. Creation, the historical Mind Maze mid-resolution premise, broader runtime work, human testing, balance, cosmology, 75-domain closure and release remain separate. No unsent rank-eight packet was reviewed from its summary.

### Return archive

**Filename:** `DD_Part5_Copied_Feat_Integration_Review_01.zip`  
**Bytes:** **36,867,306**  
**SHA256:**
```text
006c3705fa56717b4aa6b4a7fcf08e658e91a1568bbbf2b3cb8a471df42dd064
```

The final ZIP was reopened, passed CRC verification, and all **51 manifest-bound files plus the root manifest** were verified. It includes the three complete input packages and four unchanged prior correction/acceptance archives.

:chatgpt-content-reference{index="4"}[Download the SHA256 sidecar](sandbox:/mnt/data/DD_Part5_Copied_Feat_Integration_Review_01.zip.sha256)

**This completes the independent copied-feat review with exact proposed corrections. It does not claim that the remaining Ready or world-runtime work has been implemented.**
